I have the same question as @prasanthkrishnan. Additionally, the loading symbols in the bottom-left corner are causing the UI to shift in libvterm (and also in the installation script). This is a font issue, though, because `･` **(U+FF65)** is a CJK character that is not present in most Latin fonts. Given the nature of Emacs as an editor, it will fall back to a non-monospace font for that character. Similarly, `⬝` **(U+2B1D)** is also not present in most fonts, although it is not a CJK character. My current solution is to replace both characters with the _"Middle Dot"_ `·` **(U+00B7)**: ```emacs-lisp (defvar my-vterm-display-table (make-display-table)) ;; Map U+2B1D (Black Very Small Square) to display as U+00B7 (Middle Dot) (aset my-vterm-display-table ?\u2B1D (vector ?\u00B7)) ;; Map U+FF65 (Halfwidth Katakana Middle Dot) to display as U+00B7 (Middle Dot) (aset my-vterm-display-table ?\uFF65 (vector ?\u00B7)) (add-hook 'vterm-mode-hook (lambda () (setq buffer-display-table my-vterm-display-table))) ``` Preventing the use of characters that are not available in monospace fonts might fix these kinds of issues.
